cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository, so the token
# can write to pull requests opened from forks. This workflow never checks out
# or runs code from the pull request, and passes untrusted values (title,
# username) through environment variables rather than interpolating them into
# the script.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Triage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Welcome the contributor and label the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label needs-triage
          printf 'Welcome, @%s! Thanks for opening this pull request.\n\nSummary: %s\n' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$PR_TITLE" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/comment.md"
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/comment.md"
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage workflow

`.github/workflows/triage.yml` runs when a pull request is opened. It:

- posts a comment welcoming the author by username and repeating the pull request title as a summary
- applies the `needs-triage` label (create this label in the repository first, or labeling will fail)

It uses the `pull_request_target` trigger so the token has write access for pull requests opened from forks. For that reason the workflow never checks out or executes pull request code, and it passes the title and username through environment variables instead of interpolating them into the script.
EOF

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and a "Triage workflow" section in the README. I haven't run the workflow, so it's untested.

- **Trigger:** it runs on `pull_request_target` when a pull request is opened. A plain `pull_request` trigger gives forks a read-only token, so it couldn't comment or label there.
- **Comment and label:** the comment reads "Welcome, @<username>! … Summary: <PR title>", and the workflow applies `needs-triage`. Both use the `gh` CLI that's already on the runner, so there's no third-party action to pin.
- **Safety:** with `pull_request_target` the token has write access, so the workflow never checks out or runs the pull request's code. It passes the title and username through environment variables instead of putting them directly in the script. That stops a crafted title from injecting shell commands.
- **Permissions:** it asks only for `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`, scoped to the one job.
- **Label:** the `needs-triage` label has to exist in the repository first, or the labeling step will fail. The README says so.
